one_liner: Notion has a broad REST API (api.notion.com) with free self-serve tokens (PAT, internal integration), OAuth 2.0 for public integrations, webhooks, and a vendor-hosted MCP server.
auth_notes: Public integrations use OAuth (redirect URI, client ID and secret). Personal access tokens and internal integration tokens are static bearer tokens. Internal integrations are created by a workspace owner, and pages must be shared with them. The pages given don't confirm that the token endpoint uses Basic client auth, so the draft's claim about it is dropped.
access_notes: API access is included on the Free plan. A PAT can be created from the Developer portal. On Business and Enterprise, PAT creation is restricted by default until a workspace owner enables it. Internal integrations are created by a workspace owner, and a free personal workspace is enough.
blocker_notes: No significant blocker. Users must share pages with an internal integration or authorize through OAuth. PAT creation can be restricted on Business and Enterprise plans.

evidence.quote: A personal access token (PAT) lets you authenticate API requests as yourself without setting up a connection or completing an OAuth flow.
A public integration uses OAuth: you register a redirect address, receive a client ID and client secret
A workspace owner creates it, copies its token and shares pages with it by hand.
You can create an integration on any of the four plans, so your plan tier doesn't restrict your ability to build integrations
On Business and Enterprise plans, PAT creation is restricted by default.
